Novaload's LOAD routine, in the tape buffer: the boot program points the KERNAL's LOAD vector ($0330) at it, and the game's block loader ($2A62-$2AD2) reaches it through the KERNAL's LOAD. A device other than 1 (tape) goes to the KERNAL's own load at $F4A5. It starts CIA 1's timer A at $81F4, maps all RAM with I/O ($01 = $05), waits for the lead-in of 0 bits and a 1, then reads $AA, the name's length (checked against $B7) and the name (checked against ($BB)), and starts again on any mismatch. The six header bytes go to $AC-$B1 (load address with the page one before the first, end address, bytes in the last page, page count); each page follows its running checksum. Status $30 in $90 on a checksum error, 0 when done; it then waits a moment, sets $01 = $37, returns the end address in X/Y and runs IOINIT ($FF84) keeping $DD00 (the video bank). The border flashes as bytes arrive ($03DE).
`jsr $F817`, the KERNAL's "press play on tape" wait; the game's block loader writes $AD here ($2A67-$2A69), turning it into a harmless `lda $F817`, so a load asks nothing on the bitmap screen.
Adds the byte read last ($AA) to the running checksum $A3, then reads the next byte (falls into novaload_get_byte).
Reads one byte from tape, lowest bit first: starts from $7F, a marker whose 0 bit falls out into the carry after the eighth bit; returns it in A and $AA.

Waits for the next pulse (CIA 1's FLAG, bit 4 of $DC0D), reads timer A's high byte and restarts the timer from $81F4 ($DC0E = $11): a pulse longer than 500 cycles leaves bit 7 clear and reads as 1. The bit is rotated into the byte on the stack; loops until the marker comes out. Flashes the border.

Draws the two choices of state 11 (Easy or Hard): the colour of each from choice_colour ($0AF4, $0AF5) into the screen colours of a 17-cell bar at pixel (92, 19) and (92, 51), through fill_colour_block; then the sprite text panel (exit_to_sprites $0AD0).
The game's place in the show's running order: index into $3362 (whose turn), $338E/$33AE (the step's routine) at $2D1C; set at $2CDA and $3023, stepped at $2D36, set by the menu at $E5C7.

The twelve cells of the number grid, 0-11, in the order the computer picks them: shuffled by $2C45 (15 random swaps, $2C5E-$2C69) and read at $2C11, where the computer takes the first cell not yet used.
The computer's place in number_order (read $2C0E, stepped $2C19 past used cells, cleared $2CE0).

The choice each team made with fire, team 0 here and team 1 at $0760: written at $0A07 and $081A; read at $2A15 (the block to load), $2F97, $30C6 (compared with the right answer's slot $3506), $3A86-$3AB3 (easy or hard).

Non-zero when both teams answer at once (both cursors on screen): answer_cursor_frame then handles team 1 and team 0 in the same frame. Set to $FF at $0D96 and cleared at $0E7D and $0EAD; also written at $35CE and $3925.

The display state's per-frame interrupt, after irq_frame when second_irq_on is set: pushes the registers, sets the bitmap or the blank screen as irq_frame does, turns on the sprites in sprite_enable_value ($07C4), copies the state's sprite-row record (state_row_record, state_row_records) into the raster handlers' operands, and jumps to the state's routine (state_handler_lo/hi). Each routine leaves through $0BC5 or $0C47, which set the next interrupt and return from it.
Operand of `lda #$FF`: the sprites irq_state turns on ($D015); written to 0 or $FF by 18 places in the title part and 26 in the menu (byte search).
`jmp`, its address written each frame at $07FC/$0802 from state_handler_lo/hi.
Operand of state_jump, low byte (written $07FC from state_handler_lo).
Operand of state_jump, high byte (written $0802 from state_handler_hi).

Display state 9, once a frame: the "Question block 1" to "5" menu. A fire press (once fire_held is clear) sets step_done and copies the cursor (answer_cursor, 0-4) to choice; every fourth frame, before the choice, the stick moves the cursor down (to 4) or up (to 0). The five lines get screen colour $0E (light blue) for the chosen and 0 for the others in 17-cell bars at pixel X 92, Y 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 (fill_colour_block). Then the sprite text panel.
The computer's cursor is on its chosen answer: its stick becomes fire ($10).
Hands the computer's stick (cpu_stick, active high) to answer_cursor_frame as if read from a joystick: inverts it into stick and continues at $09BF.

The computer's turn in an answer choice, every fourth frame (from $09AF). First it wanders: cpu_moves times it holds a random up or down (direction_bits) for 1-2 turns (cpu_wait). Then it decides (cpu_answer_decide $0936) and steers its cursor (team 1's, $0CB9) up or down to that answer, then presses fire.
Moves the computer's cursor toward cpu_target: fire when there, else up ($2B87 = 1) when the cursor's slot number is above the target's, down (2) when below.
Counts cpu_wait down; when it runs out and moves remain (cpu_moves), picks a new wait of 1-2 turns and a random up or down.

Picks the computer's answer. Easy or Hard (display state 11): Hard (1) when the first team's score ($38A6) is ahead of the computer's ($38A7), else a random one of the two. Four answers: when the first team is ahead, the right answer's slot ($3506) with probability 192/256, else (and always when the computer is level or ahead) a random slot 0-3 other than the one the first team already chose ($2B91, $FF when none). Sets $2B84 so the decision is made once.
Stores the decision in cpu_target and marks it made ($2B84).
The answer slot the computer has decided on (written $095D, $097A; read $08EE, $08FC).
The computer's stick for answer_cursor_frame, active high (1 up, 2 down, $10 fire): written at $08D8, $090C, $0930, read at $08DB.

Non-zero makes display state 10's routine draw two choices instead of four (read $3D48, jumps to two_choice_highlight) and changes the round code at $2D44; set at $39AC, cleared at $2E15. What sets it in play is not established.

Display states 7 (four answers) and 11 (Easy or Hard), once a frame. Every fourth frame the team whose turn it is (team) moves its cursor (answer_cursor, $0CB8 + team) up or down between 0 and answer_last; the computer's team moves through cpu_answer_frame. Fire, once fire_held is clear, calls the effects code at $4FCB with X = 6 (when it is loaded, $33FE), copies the cursor to choice and sets step_done and fire_held. Until then each frame recolours the answers: the cursor's in the team's colour (team_colour $0CBE: red, blue); in the round where both teams answer ($1DC0 = 3) team 0's red, team 1's blue, purple where they meet. Then draws the colours (answer_bars_draw $0A77).
Ten bytes no code reaches, between `jmp cpu_answer_frame` and `jsr read_input`: they decode as `ldy $F9 / ldx $0CB8,Y / lda #0 / sta $0AF4,X`, which would clear the colour of the team's cursor.
The human team's turn: reads its stick (read_input).
Stores the stick and moves the team's cursor: down (bit 1 low) unless at answer_last, up (bit 0 low) unless at 0.
Operand of `cmp #$03`: the last answer slot, 3, or 1 in display state 11 (written at $0988/$0993).
Skips the fire test once step_done is set.
Fire held and fire_held clear: the choice is made. Fire released: clears fire_held.
Clears fire_held.
Sets the four answer colours (choice_colour): all 0, then the cursors' colours as answer_cursor_frame says.
One team's cursor in its colour (team_colour).
When both teams answer at once, handles team 0 after team 1 in the same frame.

Display state 11 goes to two_choice_highlight. Else fills four 23-cell bars at pixel X 70, Y 19, 35, 51, 67 with choice_colour 0-3 (fill_colour_block): answers A and C in colour RAM ($D800), B and D in the screen colours ($5C00).
Leaves a display state's routine through sprites_row0 ($0C47), which places the sprite text panel and returns from the interrupt.
state3_flash's place in flash_colours (written $0711).
state3_flash's frame counter: the colour changes every fifth frame.
The colours state3_flash cycles: 0 6 14 3 1 3 14 6 0 (black, blue, light blue, cyan, white and back), ended by $FF.
For each step of flash_colours, frames of five to hold it: 16 at white (step 4) and at black (step 8), else 0.
For each step, the value state3_flash writes to flash_mark: $FF at steps 4 and 8.
Count of the current hold in state3_flash.
Written by state3_flash ($071A) and the menu ($E8D6); no reader found in the title code or a byte search of the menu.
The menu's count of team members picked so far (read $CDBA, stepped $CDCA; written $E6E2, $E813), the index of the next slot in team_stars.

The colour of each choice's bar: four answers ($0AF4-$0AF7), five question blocks ($0AF4-$0AF8), two choices ($0AF4/$0AF5). Written by the choosers ($0A13-$0A62, $0856-$086C, $3D10-$3D45), read when the bars are drawn.
choice_colour of the second choice (answer B, Easy or Hard's Hard): written $0A21, $3D13, read $073A, $0A99, $3D69.
choice_colour of the third choice (answer C): written $0A24, $3D16, read $0AAD, $3D7D.
choice_colour of the fourth choice (answer D): written $0A27, $3D19, read $0AC1, $3D91.
choice_colour of the fifth question block (written $0864, read $08C4).
Twelve bytes, one for each star of the team-picking grid: $FF once picked (written by the menu at $CD9F,X and $E704,X, read $CD98,X, $CEDF,X).

The stars the teams picked, each as its number + 3: the four members in the order picked ($0B05-$0B08, written $CDC1,Y with Y = member_count) and the two captains ($0B09 team 0, $0B0A team 1, written $CDB4,Y with Y = team); the menu reads each to draw the faces ($C8E0-$CB9E).
team_stars: the second member picked.
team_stars: the third member picked.
team_stars: the fourth member picked.
team_stars: team 0's captain (written by the menu at $CDB4,Y; read at $C8E0, $CB80).
team_stars: team 1's captain (read by the menu at $CB9E); the round code reads team_subjects as $0B0A,Y with Y from 1.

Subjects: the specialist subject each team chose ($0B0B team 0, $0B0C team 1, written by the menu at $EA4C,X), then the four members' ($0B0D-$0B10, copied from star_subject at $CDC4-$CDC7). The round code at $3997 reads $0B0A,Y with Y 1-6 from the order at $33F0 ($3997) as the subject of the player asked.
team_subjects: the four members' subjects ($0B0D-$0B10), copied by the menu from star_subject at $CDC7,Y.
The stick bits up, down, left, right (1, 2, 4, 8): the computer's random moves take entries 0-1 (answers, $092D) or 0-3 (number grid, $2C3A).
direction_bits' left and right (4, 8), read as $0B13,X by cpu_subject_frame ($0B48).
Turns left before the computer's next random move: in answers 1-2 ($0924), in the subject choice 0-7 ($0B3F); cleared at $2DDE, $39C8 and by the menu ($E6EA).
The computer's held stick in the subject choice (inverted, written $0B4D, read $0B56).

The computer's random moves: in answers the moves left (set to 8-11 at $2DD7, counted down at $0917); in the subject choice and the number grid the moves made, counted up ($0B25, $2C04) to cpu_moves_limit or 4.
The number of random moves after which the computer picks its subject (cpu_subject_frame, $0B2B); set by the menu ($CD8D, $E5DD, $E6FD).
The last byte of each speech-bubble placement in bubble_xy ($0F, $1F), by bubble_position.

The computer choosing its specialist subject, once a frame from the menu's handler (jumped to from $EA30, returns to $EA36): holds a random left or right for 0-7 frames (cpu_wait, cpu_subject_stick); after cpu_moves_limit moves it presses fire.

Display state 5, the number grid: runs grid_cursor_frame, shows the cursor as sprite 0 doubled in both directions at grid_cursor_x/y in shape $0C ($4300), cycles its colour (grid_cursor_animate), checks fire (grid_check_fire), sets the colour, then irq_to_bottom.
Operand of `lda #$00`: the cursor sprite's colour, written by grid_cursor_animate ($1838).

Display states 4 and 6, the speech bubble: eight unexpanded sprites, shapes 0-7, colour 10, at bubble_xy's upper or lower row (bubble_position), then scrolls the text three pixels ($3671 three times) and goes to irq_to_bottom.
Operand of `lda #$00`: the bubble sprites' vertical doubling ($D017); written by the menu ($E8FC, $E924).
Operand of `lda #$0A`: the bubble sprites' colour; written by the menu ($E8F7).

Ends a display state's routine without the sprite text panel: next interrupt irq_bottom at line $D4, then pulls the registers and returns from the interrupt. Also the routine of states 8 and 12, and the exit of score_digits_frame ($205F).

Raster interrupt at line $D4, below the panel: turns off sprite doubling, turns all sprites on and, when the display state wants them (state_bottom_sprites), places the score sprites (score_xy, shapes score_shapes); gives all eight sprites the colour at $0C1E (light grey $0F unless state3_flash changes it), then chains to irq_frame at line $FA.
Operand of `lda #$0F`: the colour irq_bottom gives all sprites; written by state3_flash ($0714) and the menu ($E30E, $E70F, $E952).

Places the first row of the sprite text panel and leaves the interrupt: sprite 7 in the right half (MSB $80), Y from row0_y (sprites 3-6 one lower, 7 two lower), X from panel_x (from its second half except in display state 0), shapes $10-$17 ($4400-$45FF), then the next interrupt is irq_sprite_row1 at irq_row1_line. Display states 3, 7, 9, 10, 11 and the menu's end here.
Operand of `ldx #$84`: Y of the panel's first row, written each frame at $07D0 from state_row_records column 0.
Operand of `lda $0CF0,X`, low byte: $F8 (the second half of picture_x), or $F0 in display state 0.
Operand of `lda $0CF0,X`, high byte (always $0C).
Operand of `lda #$96`: the line irq_sprite_row1 runs on; written at $07D6 from state_row_records column 3.

The answer cursor of team 0; team 1's at $0CB9 (answer_cursor + team). Moved by answer_cursor_frame and block_choice_frame (0-4 there), cleared at $2F34 and $3A21, by the menu at $E2F6; read by the choosers and at $2921, $3D42.
Team 1's answer cursor (the computer's when it plays): read by cpu_answer_steer and the recolouring; cleared at $2F37, $3A24 and by the menu ($E2F9).
Read by the menu only, as $0CBA,X ($E9C5): 02.
Read by the menu only, as $0CBB,X ($E9CB): 00 00 06.
The two teams' cursor colours: 2 (red) for team 0, 6 (blue) for team 1 (read $0A5C).

The speech bubble's sprite positions, two placements of eight X/Y pairs: X 80, 104, 128 ... 248 at Y $50 (upper), then the same X at Y $90 (lower); state4_bubble_frame copies one placement backwards from bubble_xy_end.
X/Y pairs for the eight sprites below the panel: the score digits at X $20 and $30 (team 0) and $130, $140 (team 1, with the MSBs $0C), all at Y $E2; sprites 4-7 at 0, 0.
X of the sprite text panel's eight columns, 24 pixels apart: $58-$E8 and $100 for display state 0, then $5C-$EC and $104 for the others.
Shape numbers 0-7 for the speech bubble's sprites ($4000-$41FF).
Shape numbers for the sprites below the panel: 8-11 ($4200-$42FF, the four score digits score_digits_frame draws), then 8 for the unused four.

Shape numbers $10-$17 of the sprite text panel's first row, read by sprites_row0; the next sixteen ($18-$27, the other rows) are not read, because irq_sprite_row1 and irq_sprite_row2 load them as immediates.
picture_shapes for the second and third rows ($18-$27): not read by any code.
Text printer: the low byte of the address after the control bytes $7D and $7E (written $37EB, $3802; read $37F5, $3810).
Text printer: the high byte of a $7D call's address (written $380A, read $3815).

The number grid's fire, once a frame from state5_grid_frame: on a new press (grid_fire_latch) on a number not yet played (number_used $1D66, index grid_row * 4 + grid_column), marks it played, takes the subject behind it (number_subject $1D72) for the question ($B325, then $2C72 picks one), draws that subject's icon over the cell (colour_face_block at the cell's place from grid_cell_row/column $16BF/$16CB), colours the cell (highlight_cell: colour RAM 1, screen colours $CF), sets step_done, switches to display state 5 and calls the effects code at $4FCB with X = 5. Releasing fire clears grid_fire_latch.

Show step 16 (from the step table at $338E/$33AE): the Quickfire Round. Builds its screen ($2072, $31F8, $324E, $28C0), sets both_teams_answer, the round type ($1DC0 = 3), clears the question count ($B1DF), prints its announcement ($B2CE, "The next round is (The Quickfire Round)..."), switches to display state 6 (the bubble) with 2 points a question ($30F4, $3102), runs the per-frame routine and waits for step_done, then ends the step ($2D33).
Show steps 17-24: the next Quickfire question: bubble in its lower place, display state 8, counts the question ($B1DF), 2 points, then the question at $2DC7.

Show step 15: Name the Year, team 1's turn. Builds the screen, prints the text at $B247 (team 1's name from $B1F1, an event byte, then "'s team - What Year was this ?" from $B2B4), sets $AF3A to 2, display state 6; while the text runs, each event byte $F0 in it (text_event) calls $31D7. Then continues at round_pick_item.

Show step 14: Name the Year. Builds the screen, prints $B286 ("The next round is (Name the Year)... What Year was this ?"), sets $AF3A to 1, display state 6, calling $322D at each text event; then round_pick_item.

Shared end of the two Name the Year steps (name_the_year $0E39 and name_the_year_2 $0DFC): round type 1, both_teams_answer off, picks one of the round's eight items not used yet (bit masks round_bits $1DA7 against items_used $1DB0) into question_number, 3 points ($30F4, $3102), $1DBF = 2, and ends the step ($2D33).
Blanks the display at the next frame: clears screen_on and waits until irq_frame has copied it to irq_sync. Called by the menu ($E5B7, $E6F2, $E8C0, $E937; byte search).
Shows the bitmap from the next frame: sets screen_on and waits for irq_frame to copy it. Called by the menu ($E5B0, $E65B, $E79F, $E90F, $E975; byte search).

At the start of a game (from $2CE3): both teams' scores ($38A6, $38A7) and the scores shown ($38A4, $38A5) to 0, the score roll's counters (score_anim_1/2, $2070, $2071, $206F) cleared, and the four digit sprites' source pointers ($2067-$206E) set to $A8C9, the image of 0.

For each of the block's ten question groups, how many of its questions have not yet been asked: set to the group's size at $2AFA when a block loads, counted down by the question picker ($2C96). At 0 the picker stops checking which were asked, so the group's questions repeat.
Clears $4200-$43FF, sprite shapes 8-15 (the score digits and the grid cursor's shape); called by the menu's start-up ($E339).
Steps the text printer's pointer (text_ptr) by one; 11 calls, all in the printer ($3715-$3805).
Puts text_ptr + 1 into text_return ($F4/$F5): where a string called with $7D returns ($371B, $3742, $380D).

Operand of the same `sta`, high byte ($0F4C, $0F72).

The source's high byte (from icon_addr_hi).

Operand of `lda $17BE,X`, low byte (screen-colour source, high byte table); the menu sets $6C ($176C) at $CBF0.

The colour RAM row's high byte.

Operand of `sta $FFFF,y` at $214D: the screen-colour address ($5C00) of the clock's current row, stepped 40 a row ($215C-$216A).

High byte of the clock's screen-colour pointer at $214E; the code after it fills 64 cells with $B5, moves to the right half (column + 4) and finds its first bitmap cell (bitmap_row_lo/hi + the times-8 tables $4B00/$4A00).
Operand of `ldy $FFFF,x` at $21A4: the right half's tile list for this face, from $8F28/$8F48 ($20EB/$20F1).
High byte of the right half's tile list pointer ($8F48 + face, $20F1).
Operand of `lda $FFFF,x` at $21BC: the current tile's 8 bytes, $900A + 8 x tile ($21AD/$21B5, through the times-8 tables $4B00/$4A00).
High byte of the tile source at $21BD ($90 + the times-8 high byte, so tiles start at $900A).
Operand of `sta $FFFF,x` at $21BF: the bitmap address of the right half's current cell; +8 along a row, +$128 to the next row's first cell ($21D1-$21F3).

High byte of the right half's bitmap cell pointer; the code after it copies 32 tiles (4 a row, 8 rows), then turns to the upper left quarter: its list from $8F68/$8F88, the column back 4, and tiles 12-15, 8-11, 4-7, 0-3 in that order.
Operand of `ldy $FFFF,x` at $2246: the upper left quarter's tile list for this face, from $8F68/$8F88 ($21FF/$2205).
High byte of the upper left quarter's tile list pointer ($8F88 + face, $2205).
Operand of `lda $FFFF,x` at $225F: the current tile's bytes for the upper left quarter ($224F/$2257).

High byte of the upper left quarter's tile source; the loop after it stores each tile's 8 bytes mirrored (through $B700) into the row buffer $8FE8 from its end backwards, so the row comes out reversed.
Operand of `sta $FFFF,x` at $2285: the bitmap address of the upper left quarter's current cell ($2217-$2233, stepped at $2292-$22C3).

High byte of the upper left quarter's bitmap cell pointer; the code after it copies the 32-byte row buffer into 4 cells, does the 4 rows, then sets the lower left quarter's list ($8FA8/$8FC8) and row + 4.
Operand of `ldy $FFFF,x` at $2318: the lower left quarter's tile list for this face, from $8FA8/$8FC8 ($22D1/$22D7).
High byte of the lower left quarter's tile list pointer ($8FC8 + face, $22D7).
Operand of `lda $FFFF,x` at $2331: the current tile's bytes for the lower left quarter ($2321/$2329).
High byte of the lower left quarter's tile source; the same reversing and mirroring copy into $8FE8 as at $225F.
Operand of `sta $FFFF,x` at $2357: the bitmap address of the lower left quarter's current cell ($22E9-$2305, stepped at $2364-$2395).
High byte of the lower left quarter's bitmap cell pointer; the code after it copies each mirrored row into the bitmap, 4 rows, and returns.
Low bytes of the digit graphics of the number grid's twelve numbers ($8390, $83B0 ... $84F0, 32 bytes each); index the number 0-11, read by draw_grid_number at $23BD. High bytes at grid_number_hi.
High bytes of the number grid's digit graphics ($83 for numbers 0-3, $84 for 4-11); read at $23C3.

Draws one number of the Jukebox grid, A = 0-11, at cell_row/cell_column: colour RAM of the 4 x 4 block from the 16 bytes at $8080, then copies the number's 32 bytes of digit graphics (grid_number_lo/hi) into the middle cells of the blank ball picture at $8000 ($8028, $8030, $8048, $8050) and draws that picture's 16 cells into the bitmap. Saves and restores X and Y (draw_save_x/y). One caller, the grid redraw at $360D, for every number not yet played.
Operand of `sta $FFFF,y` at $2416: colour RAM address of the number's block row, stepped 40 a row ($2425-$2433).
High byte of the colour RAM pointer at $2417 ($D8 + row_addr_hi); the loop after it copies the 16 colours at $8080 into the 4 x 4 block.
Operand of `lda $83F0,x` at $243D: the number's first 8 bytes of digit graphics (grid_number_lo/hi, $23C0/$23C6); $2444, $244A and $2450 are the next three 8-byte pieces.
High byte of the first digit-graphics source ($23C6, from grid_number_hi).
Operand of `lda $83F8,x` at $2443: the number's second piece of digit graphics (+8, $23CF/$23D7).
High byte of the second digit-graphics source (carry of +8, $23D2-$23D7).
Operand of `lda $8400,x` at $2449: the third piece (+16, $23E0/$23E8).
High byte of the third digit-graphics source (carry of +16, $23E3-$23E8).
Operand of `lda $8408,x` at $244F: the fourth piece (+24, $23F1/$23F9).
High byte of the fourth digit-graphics source; the loop after it copies the 4 x 8 bytes into the ball picture, then works out the bitmap address of cell_row/cell_column.
Operand of `lda $FFFF,x` at $248B: the ball picture's current cell, from $8000 a cell at a time ($247D-$2484, +8 at $24C3-$24D1).
High byte of the ball picture source at $248C ($80, so the picture is read from $8000).
Operand of `sta $FFFF,x` at $248E: the bitmap address of the ball's current cell (bitmap_row + 8 x column, $245A-$247A), +8 along a row, +$128 to the next.
High byte of the ball's bitmap pointer; the loop after it copies 16 cells of 8 bytes, 4 a row, and returns with X and Y restored.

Count-down shared by the question block's searches: question records left to skip in find_question ($24DE, $2523), strings left in find_spare_answer ($2559, $2587), words left in find_word ($259C, $25C3).
find_question's count of $FF bytes passed: odd after a question's end, even after its answer's end, which closes a record ($24E3, $2519-$251C).

Finds question record X of the loaded block. Sets the word list pointer (word_list_lo/hi, $34/$35) to $B800 + the offset in $B802 (high) / $B803 (low), then walks the records from $B80F: each is the question ending $FF, the answer ending $FF, then 4 bytes (a flags byte and three wrong-answer numbers, read by build_answers). Returns zp_2E/zp_2F at the start of question X's text (for X > 0 the byte after the previous record's 4 trailing bytes; for X = 0 it returns $B814, which is why build_question special-cases question 0 and starts it at $B80F). 4 callers: $342C (the question), $3B45, $3B91, $3BDD (a wrong answer borrowed from another question).
Operand of `lda $FFFF` at $2507: find_question's scan pointer through the records, from $B80F ($24F7/$24FE), +1 a byte, +5 past each record's closing $FF and its 4 trailing bytes ($2528-$2536).
High byte of find_question's scan pointer ($B8 at $24FE); the loop after it counts $FF bytes and records, then returns zp_2E/zp_2F 5 bytes past the last record's closing $FF.

Points zp_ptr_2A at string X of the block's list of spare wrong answers, which lies at $B800 + the offset in $B800 (high) / $B801 (low); for X = 0 the list's start. Also sets zp_2C/zp_2D to zp_ptr_2A + 1 as it was on entry (the next byte of the record's trailer). Used by build_answers when a trailer flag bit is set (3 callers, $3B3F, $3B8B, $3BD7). In block 1 $B800/$B801 are 0 and no flag bit is set in its 255 records (checked on the quiz snapshot).
Operand of `lda $FFFF` at $2575: find_spare_answer's scan pointer, from the list's start ($2562/$256C).
High byte of find_spare_answer's scan pointer ($B8 + the offset's high byte, $2567-$256C); the loop after it skips X strings and returns zp_ptr_2A after the last $FF passed.

Points zp_2E/zp_2F at word Y of the current word list (word_list_lo/hi): skips Y strings ending $FF. Words are what a byte $80 + n in a question or answer stands for. 2 callers: build_question ($3447) and write_answer ($3C9D).
Operand of `lda $FFFF` at $25B1: find_word's scan pointer from word_list_lo/hi ($25A1/$25A8).
High byte of find_word's scan pointer (word_list_hi, $25A6); the loop after it skips Y words and returns zp_2E/zp_2F after the last $FF passed.

Low bytes of the question builder for each round type ($1DC0), read by build_round_question at $2631: types 0 (Your Scene and the Jukebox) and 3 (Quickfire) $04, types 1 (Name the Year) and 2 (Spot the Star) $97.
High bytes of the same: $34 for types 0 and 3 (build_question, $3404), $26 for types 1 and 2 (build_clue_question, $2697). Read at $2637.
build_clue_question's four answer strings, low bytes (written by find_item_answers at $2675; $25E0 is the right answer, read at $2796, $25E1-$25E3 the three wrong ones).
Low byte of the item's second answer string (a wrong one), written by find_item_answers, read at $27A6.
Low byte of the item's third answer string (wrong), read at $27B6.
Low byte of the item's fourth answer string (wrong), read at $27C6.
High bytes of the four answer strings (written at $267D): $25E4 the right answer's, read at $279B.
High byte of the item's second answer string, read at $27AB.
High byte of the item's third answer string, read at $27BB.
High byte of the item's fourth answer string, read at $27CB.
Low bytes of four answer buffers for a "What happened next ?" screen, $B600, $B655, $B6AA and $7F40 (high bytes at $25EC); read only by the unreached copy_to_wnh_buffer ($2640).
High bytes of the four "What happened next" buffers ($B6, $B6, $B6, $7F), read at $2646.

Addresses of the four `$7D` call operands in wnh_text ($2615, $261B, $2621, $2627; low bytes here, high bytes at $25F4-$25F7). No instruction in the title, menu or quiz code reads them (references search and a byte-pair search).

Text in the printer's format, "What happened next ?     A. " then calls of the four buffers $B600, $B655, $B6AA, $7F40 for answers A-D, then $7F (end), and 4 zero bytes. Nothing points at it (byte-pair search of all three parts): a round of the television show (What happened next) that the game's step table ($338E) never runs.

Builds the question for the current round type: jumps (self-modified `jmp` at $263D) to round_builder_lo/hi[round_type]: build_question ($3404) for the Jukebox, Your Scene and Quickfire questions, build_clue_question ($2697) for Name the Year and Spot the Star. One caller, $2E38 in ask_question.
Operand of `jmp` at $263D: low byte of the round's builder (round_builder_lo, $2634).
High byte of the builder's address (round_builder_hi, $263A).

Copies the built text in $B500 (X bytes, with an $FF written after them) into "What happened next" buffer Y (wnh_buffer_lo/hi). No call, jump or pointer reaches it in any part (references and byte-pair searches): it belongs with the unused wnh_text.
Operand of `sta $FFFF,x` at $2654: the chosen "What happened next" buffer (wnh_buffer_lo/hi[Y], $2643/$2649).
High byte of the "What happened next" buffer address at $2655 (wnh_buffer_hi[Y], $2649); the loop after it copies X + 1 bytes down to 0.

For build_clue_question: from the $FF that ends an item's third clue (pointer at $265E), stores the starts of the next four strings (the right answer, then three wrong ones) in clue_answer_lo/hi, and sets the word list (word_list_lo/hi) to $F200 + the offset in $F202 (high) / $F203 (low). One caller ($2790).
Operand of `lda $FFFF` at $265D: find_item_answers' scan pointer (from $2706/$2715, then $2787/$278D).
High byte of find_item_answers' scan pointer; the loop after it records four string starts and sets the section's word list from $F202/$F203.

Name the Year and Spot the Star: which of the item's three clues is shown, 0-2. Cleared for each new question at $2DC9; read by build_clue_question ($2726, $2743) and by ask_again ($2DEF) to pick "First/Second/Final clue - " (table $B24F/$B252); raised when the clock runs out ($2FCD), and at 3 the question is over ($2FD3).
build_clue_question's counter: items passed while finding question_number's item ($26C6-$26F6), then strings passed while finding the clue and the end of the third clue ($2723-$277E).

Round types 1 and 2 (through build_round_question): builds the clue as the question and the item's four answers. Shuffles the answer slots (shuffle_answers), takes the section's items: Name the Year at $F204, Spot the Star at $F200 + the offset in $F200 (high) / $F201 (low); each item is 7 strings ending $FF (three clues, the right answer, three wrong answers), and question_number (0-7) picks the item. Points build_question's source ($343C) at clue clue_number, has find_item_answers find the four answers and the section's word list ($F200 + $F202/$F203), builds the clue into $B500 with "." for its last character (build_question_text, $34E4 = $2E), and writes the answers into the answer buffers by slot (write_answer: the right one into slot $3506). Reads the block's section C at $F200-$FFFF, which needs no bank switch.
Operand of `lda $FFFF` at $26D0: the scan through the section's items, from $F204 or $F200 + offset ($26A6-$26C1).

High byte of the item scan pointer at $26D1 ($F2 + the offset's high byte, or $F2); the loop after it skips 7 strings an item until question_number items are passed, then hands the item's start to the clue and answer scans and to build_question's source ($343C).
Operand of `lda $FFFF` at $272E: the scan from the item's first clue to clue clue_number ($2709/$2718).
High byte of the clue scan pointer at $272F; the loop after it skips clue_number strings and points build_question's source at that clue.
Operand of `lda $FFFF` at $2765: the scan from the chosen clue to the $FF that ends the third clue ($270F/$271E, $2754/$275F).

High byte of the scan pointer at $2766; the code after it finds the end of the third clue, has find_item_answers collect the answers, builds the clue (build_question_text) and writes the four answers into their slots (write_answer, X = $3506-$3509).

Show step 31: the end of the game. Builds the screen, then prints "That was the last round of (Pop Quiz)." and either "The game was tied - congratulations to both teams" ($B391, when the BCD scores $38A6 and $38A7 are equal) or "Congratulations to <winner's team> and commiserations to <loser's team>" ($B3C8; the two `$7D` call operands at $B3DF and $B3F9 are set to the team names $B1E7 or $B1F1), then "Thank you for playing the game - For a new game press fire" and the text's `$7C` wait for either player's fire. In the bubble (display state 6) it waits for the text to end, then starts a new game at new_game ($2CD8). Reached only through the step table.

Puts the slot numbers 0-3 in answer_slots ($3506-$3509) and swaps two random entries 9 times (random from $3DA3). $3506 is then the slot (0 A, 1 B, 2 C, 3 D) of the right answer and $3507-$3509 those of the wrong ones. 2 callers: build_clue_question ($269C), build_answers ($3AF6).

At a game's start ($2CE9): the Jukebox grid's twelve numbers get the subjects 0-5 twice (number_subject $1D72, positions 0-5 and 6-11) and are marked unplayed (number_used $1D66), then 15 random swaps of two of the twelve subjects. So which number hides which subject changes every game.

Draws the studio frame's tiles (draw_frame_tiles with tile_row_offset 0) and the tile block at row 6, column $12 (draw_tile_block). 7 callers, the start of every round's screen ($0D91, $0DFF, $0E3C, $3587, $38AC, $38E9, $3977).

Clears the colours of six blocks along row 3 (columns 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 27: the subjects' icons), clears 150 bitmap cells from $62D0 (clear_bitmap_cells), sets answer_cursor to 0 and clears the sprite text panel (clear_panel). 3 callers: block_choice ($292C, $2A12) and the Easy-or-Hard choice ($39DD).

Asks which question block to load and loads it. From new_game when the block's games are used up (games_left $2B90 below 0; the menu sets it to 0, so the first game asks). Prints "Question block 1" to "5" (print_text 31-35) in the sprite panel with alternating colour bars, runs display state 9 (block_choice_frame $0808) until fire, then with the interrupt off loads through the KERNAL: messages off, Novaload's "press play" call patched to `lda` (tape_play_call), device 1; the file "FX" (the sound effects), then the block's three one-letter files (block_file_letters: block 1 A, B, C ... block 5 M, N, O); the first is copied from $E000-$EFFF to $D000-$DFFF with all RAM mapped ($01 = $34). Then games_left = 3 (so a block serves four games), the question groups from the block header (11 bytes from $B804 to group_first $1D7E; group sizes, questions left and random masks of 7, 15, 31 or 63), clears items_used and items_used_2 (Name the Year and Spot the Star items, two of each a game), sets $33FE (effects loaded) and falls into irq_setup.
Operand of `ldx #$73` at $2A83: low byte of the first file's name (block_file_letters + block_file_offset[choice], $2A1E).
Operand of `ldy #$2B` at $2A85: high byte of the first file's name ($2A25).
Operand of `ldx #$74` at $2ABB: low byte of the second file's name (first + 1, $2A2E).
Operand of `ldy #$2B` at $2ABD: high byte of the second file's name ($2A36).
Operand of `ldx #$75` at $2AC9: low byte of the third file's name (second + 1, $2A3F).

Operand of `ldy #$2B` at $2ACB: high byte of the third file's name ($2A47); the code after it loads the third file, sets the border black and games_left, and copies the block header into the question groups.

Starts the game's interrupts: $01 = $25, CIA 1's interrupts off, NMI vector $FFFA = $0BE6, IRQ vector $FFFE = $07A4, CIA 2 port A to output on bits 0-5 and $DD00 = $96 (VIC bank 1, $4000-$7FFF), $D018 = $78; initialises the sound effects ($5095) when they are loaded ($33FE), else the music ($4C00 with A = 0); raster interrupt at line $FC. Called by the menu at $E330 (byte search) and reached at the end of block_choice.
For each question block 0-4 (choice), the offset of its three file letters in block_file_letters: 0, 3, 6, 9, 12. Read at $2A18.
The question blocks' file names, one letter each, three a block: "ABC" block 1, "DEF" 2, "GHI" 3, "JKL" 4, "MNO" 5 (loaded in that order by block_choice, $2A81-$2AD2).
"FX", the 2-letter name of the sound-effects file block_choice loads first (SETNAM with $2B82 at $2A73-$2A79).

The computer has chosen: number grid, set when it has picked its target number ($2C2E, read $2B9A); answers, set by its decision ($0960, $097D, read $08E6); also read by the computer's subject choice ($0B20). Cleared for each choice ($2DE1, $35F5, $39CB).
Joystick bits the computer holds to move along a grid row: $04 left (target to the left), $08 right. Indexed by grid_move_right ($2BF3).
Joystick bits for moving between rows: $01 up, $02 down. Indexed by grid_move_down ($2BE7) and by the computer's answer moves ($0909).
Column (0-3) of the number the computer has picked (index & 3, $2C25); read at $2BCD.
Row (0-2) of the number the computer has picked (index / 4, $2C2B); read at $2BB3.
1 when the computer's target is to the right of the cursor ($2BD9), 0 to the left or level ($2BC7); indexes stick_left_right.
1 when the target is below the cursor ($2BBF), 0 above or level ($2BAD); indexes stick_up_down. Also used by the computer's answer moves ($08F5-$0906).
Columns between the cursor and the computer's target ($2BDC); compared with grid_row_distance to move along the longer way first.
Rows between the cursor and the target ($2BC2, read $2BDF).
The number (0-11) the computer is steering to (from number_order, $2C20); when the cursor's index equals it, the computer presses fire ($2BA6).
Games left before a new question block is chosen: 3 after a load ($2AE0), decremented at each new game ($2CEF); below 0 calls block_choice. The menu sets it to 0 ($E5D2).
Player one's answer for the computer to avoid: $FF at each step ($2D19), player one's choice when team 0 answers ($2F9A); compared by the computer's answer choice ($094B).
The computer presses fire on the grid: stick becomes $EF (bit 4, fire, clear: the inverted form the hardware gives). Reached from $2BA9 when the cursor is on the target.

The computer's move in the Jukebox number grid (jumped to from $05FA): three random stick moves (direction_bits), counted in cpu_moves; on its fourth turn it takes the next unplayed number in its shuffled order (number_order $0752 from number_pick) as the target; after that it steers the cursor toward the target, the longer distance first (stick_left_right/stick_up_down), and presses fire on it ($2B92). The fake stick goes to grid_stick_dir.
At a game's start ($2CEC): 15 random swaps of two of the twelve entries of number_order ($0752), the order in which the computer picks grid numbers.

Picks a question of group A (subject 0-5) into question_number: a random number below group_size (masked with group_mask, redrawn when too big) plus group_first. While the group's subject_left ($0F09) is not 0 it counts it down and redraws if the question's bit is set in asked_questions ($1DC1, bit question & 7 of byte question / 8, through round_bits), else sets the bit. subject_left counts every draw, the redrawn ones too, so once it reaches 0 questions can repeat even if some of the group were never asked. Keeps X ($2CB0). 3 callers: the grid ($0D51), Your Scene ($3AAE), Quickfire (pick_quickfire_question $3AC8).
Operand of `ldx #$00` at $2CAF: pick_question's X on entry (saved at $2C72), restored on return.
Zeroes $8000-$89FF (10 pages). No call, jump or pointer reaches it (references and byte-pair searches of all three parts).

Starts a game (jumped to by the menu at $E997, byte search, and by game_over at $2846): show_step = 0, the round-player counter $33EF = 0, number_pick = 0, both scores and their digits reset (scores_reset, score_digits_frame), a new grid (grid_setup) and computer order (shuffle_number_order); counts games_left down and, below 0, has block_choice load a question block. Then runs the show's steps from run_show_step.

Runs show step show_step ($0751, 0-31): display state 8, no state interrupt, bubble in its upper place, fire_held set, sprites off, 2 points ($30F4/$3102), team0_choice $FF; sets team from step_team ($3362) and jumps (self-modified `jmp` at $2D30) to the step's routine from step_routine_lo/hi ($338E/$33AE). A step ends at next_step, through ask_question and the answer.
Operand of `jmp` at $2D30: the step's routine, low byte from step_routine_lo ($2D27), high byte at $2D32 from step_routine_hi ($2D2D).
High byte of the step routine's address in the `jmp` at $2D30 (step_routine_hi, written $2D2D).
Where a step goes once its question is chosen (5 jumps: $0DDA Quickfire, $0EB0 Name the Year, $3660 Jukebox, $3957 Spot the Star, $3AB9 Your Scene): jumps to ask_question_body.
Counts show_step up and runs the next step (run_show_step). Reached from the end of an answer: $30AB (no one scored) and $311B (after the score roll).

Sets the question screen: for the Jukebox (round type 0 without two_choices_flag) four pauses of display state 8 (pause_frames); sprites 0-3 on, clears the play colours and two bitmap strips ($AB41 at $62A8 and $63E8), draws the centre (draw_centre); in the Quickfire Round both captains' pictures (1 at column 1, 2 at column 33), otherwise the picture in $AF3A on the side of the team whose turn it is. Then the first clue (clue_number = 0) and ask_again.
clue_number = 0, then ask_again. Also the Quickfire Round's next question jumps here ($0DF9).

Puts the question in the bubble: clears the bubble (clear_bubble), sets the computer's 8-11 wandering moves (cpu_moves), clears step_done, cpu_wait and cpu_decided, and points text_ptr at the question's lead-in: Name the Year and Spot the Star "First/Second/Final clue - " (table $B24F/$B252 by clue_number); Quickfire "Question number <n> on <subject> music - " ($B1CE); Your Scene, once, "An Easy question on" or "A Hard question on <subject> music - " ($B174/$B18B by $3ACB, clearing two_choices_flag); the Jukebox "<subject> music - " ($B324). Each lead-in continues at the built question in $B500. Then builds the question (build_round_question) and its answers (build_answers), starts the printer (text_print $36B0), shows the bubble (display state 6) and waits for the text's end.

Shows the four answers and runs the clock: clears the sprite panel and the answer area's colours (rows 11-15 columns 6-33, row 16 columns 11-29), prints the answer buffers $1BBA-$1BFF in the panel (print_text 23-26), alternate colour bars, clears clock_time unless it is the Quickfire Round (there one clock runs through all its questions), cursors to answer A, display state 7 (answer_cursor_frame). Then the clock loop: draws clock face clock_time (draw_clock at column 16, row 14), a tick sound every third loop (effects $4FCB with X = 3, Y = 1, counter $1845), and every clock_rate loops ($8F27 counts) the next face; after face 31 the time is up (time_up). When fire chooses an answer (step_done) it keeps player one's choice in team0_choice and judges it (judge_answer). Also re-entered from bonus_question ($3099).

Operand of `lda #$00` at $2F55, the face draw_clock shows: 0-31, counted up at $2F7D every clock_rate loops; 32 means time is up ($2F83). Cleared for each question at $2EF7 except in the Quickfire Round, and by the Quickfire start ($0DA0), the Jukebox step ($35D1) and Your Scene ($3A1E).

Operand of `cmp #$04` at $2F71: clock loops per clock face. 4 (the snapshot's value; set again by the final Jukebox's opening $356E), 8 for the Quickfire Round ($0DA8), so its one clock runs twice as slowly.

The clock ran out: display state 8, clears the bubble, the answers' colours and blocks, redraws the centre, effects $4FCB with X = 8, Y = 1. In Name the Year and Spot the Star with clues left (clue_number below 3, and the first try): one point less and ask_again with the next clue. Otherwise prints "Time out." with the other team's name and " for a bonus point." ($1E80 or $1E8C), switches team; in the Quickfire Round "End of Quickfire round." ($1E9D) and show_step = 24, so the round ends; on a first try the other team gets the question for a bonus point (bonus_question); on a bonus try only "Time out." ($1E97).
Time ran out on a bonus try: "Time out." without a bonus offer ($1E97), then end_step_text.

The other team gets the same question for 1 point (points = 1): tries_left ($1DBF) counts down, and when none is left the step ends (end_step_text). Otherwise in the bubble (display state 4) the text's events show the team's captain: event 0 clears the picture at column 1 row 1 and draws picture 2 (team 1's captain) at column 33, event 1 clears the one at column 33 and draws picture 1 (team 0's) at column 1. At the text's end text_ptr = $B500 and the answers and clock run again (show_answers at $2E53) for the new team.
Starts the text in text_ptr, shows the bubble (display state 4), waits for its end and goes to the next step (next_step). The ending of an unanswered question.

Judges an answer: flashes the chosen answer (flash_choice), clears the answers' colours and blocks, redraws the centre, clears the bubble. If choice[team] equals the right answer's slot ($3506): prints "Correct" with the points ($1DE1/$1DE4 by points - 1), effects $4FCB X = 4, Y = 1, and award_points. Else wrong_answer.

Starts the result text, adds the points (the `adc #` operand at $30F4 for team 0, $3102 for team 1) to the team's BCD score ($38A6 or $38A7) in decimal mode, waits for the text in the bubble (display state 4), then rolls the score digits (display state 13, score_digits_frame) and goes to the next step.

Operand of `adc #$02` at $30F3: the points a correct answer adds to team 0's score, and (less one) the index of the "Correct, n point(s)" text ($30CE). Written with points_team1 every time: 2 at each step's start ($2D11) and by the Quickfire Round ($0DC4, $0DF3), 3 by Name the Year and Spot the Star ($0EA0, $394D) and one less per clue ($2FD7), choice + 1 by Your Scene (1 Easy, 2 Hard, $3A8C), 1 for a bonus ($302B, $313D).
Operand of `adc #$02` at $3101: the points a correct answer adds to team 1's score; always written together with points_team0 ($0DC7, $0DF6, $0EA3, $2D14, $2FDA, $302E, $3140, $3950, $3A8F).

A wrong answer, with the effects $4FCB X = 1, Y = 1 and X = 2, Y = 2. In the Quickfire Round the other team gets a point at once: "Incorrect. A bonus point to <the other team>." ($1E2A, its call operand $1E46 set to that team's name $B1E7 or $B1F1), points = 1, team switched, award_points. In other rounds on a first try "Incorrect. <other team> for a bonus point." ($1EBA or $1EC5) and bonus_question; on a bonus try only "Incorrect." ($1ED0).
Display state 12, then pause_frames' delay. Called three times by the menu ($E8AC-$E8B2, byte search).
Display state 8, then a busy loop of 65,536 turns of `dex`/`bne` (about a third of a second). 4 calls from ask_question_body ($2D4E-$2D57) before a Jukebox question.

Display state 10 (answer_flash_frame $3CFC flashes the chosen answer in the team's colours) for two busy-loop delays of 65,536 turns, then display state 8. 2 callers: judge_answer ($30AE), Your Scene after Easy or Hard ($3A81).

Clears the colours of the left team's three pictures (blocks at column 3 row 9, column 1 row 1, column 6 row 17), leaving the right team's. 2 callers, the text events of Name the Year's second question ($0E30) and Spot the Star's second ($38DD).

Draws the left team's pictures: 1 at column 3 row 9, 3 at column 1 row 1, 4 at column 6 row 17, and picture 0 at column 17 row 10 (draw_frame_block). 7 callers, every round screen ($0D8B, $0E02, $0E3F, $3590, $38AF, $38EC, $397A) and the menu at $E8EF (byte search).

Clears the colours of the right team's three pictures (column 31 row 9, column 33 row 1, column 28 row 17). 2 callers, the text events of Name the Year's first question ($0E6D) and Spot the Star's first ($391A).
Draws the right team's pictures: 2 at column 31 row 9, 5 at column 33 row 1, 6 at column 28 row 17, and picture 0 at column 17 row 10. 7 callers ($0D8E, $0E05, $0E42, $358D, $38B2, $38EF, $397D).
Clears the colours of four blocks at columns 15 and 19, rows 15 and 16 (clear_block_colours). 2 callers: time_up ($2FAE), judge_answer ($30B4).
Draws picture 0 at column 17 row 17 and the frame tiles at row offset 8 (draw_frame_tiles), then the tile block at row 14 column $12 (draw_tile_block). 3 callers: $2D78, $2FB1, $30B7.
Sets the four answer bars' colours to 0 (fill_colour_block, 23 cells at X $46, Y $13, $23, $33, $43, colour RAM and screen colours in turn). 2 callers: time_up ($2FAB), judge_answer ($30B1).

print_text's table of 39 texts, low bytes (read at $1950; high bytes at print_text_hi $333B), indexed by its A. Entries 23-26 are the answer buffers $1BBA, $1BD1, $1BE8, $1BFF (show_answers), 31-35 "Question block 1" to "5" at $1C3A-$1C7E (block_choice), 36-38 "Easy", "or", "Hard" at $1C8F, $1C94, $1C97 (Your Scene); 27-30 "Answer A" to "D" at $1C16-$1C31; the rest point at $1BA1, $1BBA and texts at $CC0D-$CD14 in the menu's range.
High bytes of print_text's 39 text addresses (read at $1956).

For each show step 0-31, the team whose turn it is (read at $2D1F into team): 0 1 0 1 0 1 (Jukebox), 0 1 (Spot the Star), 0 1 0 1 0 1 (Your Scene), 0 1 (Name the Year), 0 x9 (Quickfire, both teams answer), 0 1 0 1 0 1 (final Jukebox), 0 (game over). show_step never passes 31 (game_over starts a new game), so the 12 bytes after it at $3382-$338D (00 02 00 00 05 00 00 02 00 00 05 00) are not read through this table.

Low bytes of each show step's routine (read at $2D24; high bytes at step_routine_hi): step 0 $3558 (Jukebox opening), 1-5 $357C (Jukebox), 6 $38E6 and 7 $38A9 (Spot the Star), 8 $395A (Your Scene opening), 9-13 $3965 (Your Scene), 14 $0E39 and 15 $0DFC (Name the Year), 16 $0D88 (Quickfire opening), 17-24 $0DDD (Quickfire questions 2-9), 25 $3563 (final Jukebox opening), 26-30 $357C (Jukebox), 31 $27D7 (game over).
High bytes of each show step's routine address (read at $2D2A).

Of the six players' pictures (1-6, places player_column/player_row), clears the colours of every one except $AF3A, the player whose turn it is, so only that player is left lit. Keeps Y in the operand at $33EA. 2 callers, from the text event of the Jukebox ($35BD) and Your Scene ($39B7) openings.
Operand of `ldy #$00` at $33E9: show_turn_player's loop counter (6 down to 1), kept across clear_block_colours ($33DF).

Which entry of turn_players is next: 0 at a new game ($2CDD) and at the final Jukebox's opening ($3565); counted up by each Jukebox step ($359F) and Your Scene step ($399D), so the 6 Jukebox and 6 Your Scene questions go to the six players in turn.

The picture number (1-6) of the player asked at each Jukebox or Your Scene question, by turn_player_count: 3 5 4 6 1 2 3 5 4 6 1 2 (left team 3, 4, 1; right team 5, 6, 2, alternating as the step table's teams). Read at $3596 and $398A into $AF3A, the name and event arguments of the round's text.
The column of the chosen subject's icon in Your Scene, by team: 32 for team 0, 4 for team 1 (read at $3A45).

1 once block_choice has loaded the sound effects file ($2B21); 0 in the snapshot. Read by irq_frame ($0691, effects $4F00 instead of the music $4C03), the answer choice ($09F6, effects only when loaded) and irq_setup ($2B53, initialise effects or music).
0, 7, 14: the SID register offsets of voices 1-3, read by the music driver at $4C16 (lda $33FF,x).
Where the printer goes on after an inserted name: the byte after the `$F1 n` pair, low byte (written $37AA, read at $375D on the name's `$FE`).
High byte of the address after an inserted name (written $37B1, read at $3762).

The builder for Jukebox, Your Scene and Quickfire questions (through build_round_question). Stops the state interrupt, sets irq_exit_port to $24 and waits until an interrupt has left $01 with all RAM ($01 & 7 = 4), so the block's data under the I/O area ($D000-$DFFF) can be read. Then ($3416) end character "?", the source at question question_number: $B80F for question 0, else find_question; and build_question_text. build_answers switches back.

Builds a question from its source (the operand at $343C) into $B500 for the bubble: plain bytes copied; a byte $80 + n inserts word n of the word list (find_word) with a space before it unless one is there, and a space after it; a space is put after "(" and before ")"; at the source's $FF a space and the end character ($34E4: "?" or "." for a clue), the first letter made capital, 18 spaces (so the end scrolls out of the bubble) and $7F (end of text). 2 callers: build_question ($3429) and build_clue_question ($2793).

Operand of `lda $B80F` at $343B: the question's source pointer, low byte (from build_question at $3421/$3431 or build_clue_question at $270C/$2757), +1 a byte ($34C2-$34C8). After the build it points at the question's $FF, which build_answers uses to find the answer ($3AF9).
High byte of the question's source pointer ($3426, $3436, $271B, $2762, $34CB-$34D0; read by build_answers at $3B01).
Operand of `lda $FFFF,y` at $3467: the word being inserted (from find_word, $344C/$3451).
High byte of the inserted word's address; the loop after it copies the word's letters, adds a space after a "(", and the code after it handles ")", "(" and the end of the question.
Operand of `lda #$3F` at $34E3: the question's last character, "?" ($3F, set at $3418) or "." ($2E, set by build_clue_question at $2699).

The slot (0-3: A-D) of the right answer, from shuffle_answers; $3507-$3509 hold the wrong answers' slots. Read by build_answers ($3B08) and build_clue_question ($27A0), judge_answer ($30C9) and the computer's answer choice ($095A).
The slot of the first wrong answer (shuffle_answers $284F; read $27B0, $3B71).
The slot of the second wrong answer (shuffle_answers $2853; read $27C0, $3BBD).
The slot of the third wrong answer (shuffle_answers $2857; read $27D0, $3BFC).
A counter shared by short loops: swaps left in shuffle_answers (9, $285C), grid_setup and shuffle_number_order (15, $2895, $2C47), and the strings of an item in build_clue_question ($26C9-$26EE).

The question's flags byte (the first of the 4 bytes after its answer, $3B21): bit 0, 1, 2 set means wrong answer 1, 2, 3 is a string of the spare list (find_spare_answer), clear means it is the answer of the question with that number. Read at $3B38, $3B84, $3BD0.
Zeroes 150 bitmap cells (8 bytes each), 18 cells a row, from the address X (high) / Y (low): rows step 320 bytes. 2 callers: clear_choice_area ($291C, from $62D0) and Your Scene ($3974, from $6428).
Operand of `sta $FFFF,x` at $351C: the cell being cleared, low byte (Y on entry, +8 a cell, +$B8 from a row's last cell to the next row's first).
High byte of the cell being cleared (X on entry, $3513).
Show step 0: text_ptr = $AEF5 ("The first round of the game is the Jukebox round.", then the turn's "<name> will you please make a selection.") and jukebox_question.

Show step 25: the last round. Restarts turn_player_count, team 0, clock_rate back to 4 (the Quickfire Round set 8), text_ptr = $AEB6 ("For the final round of (Pop Quiz), it's back to the Jukebox.") and jukebox_question. The grid is not reset, so the six numbers left from the first round are played.
Show steps 1-5 and 26-30: text_ptr = $AF29 ("Jukebox round - <name>, will you please make a selection.") and jukebox_question.

One Jukebox turn: clears the colours, draws the frame, clears the bubble, draws both teams; the player of this turn (turn_players[turn_player_count], counted up) goes into $AF3A and $AF3C, the name and event arguments of the text at $AF39. Prints the text in the bubble (display state 6); on its event lights only that player (show_turn_player). Then round type 0, both_teams_answer off, clock_time 0, tries_left 2, the computer's grid state cleared; redraws the grid: each unplayed number as a numbered ball (draw_grid_number), each played one as its subject's icon (colour_face_block) with the cell highlighted (highlight_cell, colour 1, $CF); runs the number grid (display state 5: grid_check_fire picks the question, cpu_grid_move plays for the computer) until a number is chosen, then ask_question.

Here `lda turn_players,x` reads the turn's player. The address $3596 is also the base of bubble_scroll's `ldx $3596,y` at $050C, which with Y = $EB-$FF reads bubble_line_offsets ($3681-$3695), not this code.
Zeroes the speech bubble's sprite shapes 0-7 ($4000-$41FF). 4 callers in the title code ($2DCC, $2FA8, $30BA, $358A) and the menu at $E336 (byte search).

One pixel of the speech bubble, called three times a frame by the bubble's display states 4 and 6 ($0BBC-$0BC2): while wait_fire_flag is set, checks fire again (wait_fire_text); otherwise the next pixel column of the current glyph (glyph_pixel_step) and scrolls the bubble one pixel (bubble_scroll).
$FF while a text's `$7C` waits for fire and neither player has pressed ($37DC); 0 once one has ($37C5). Read by bubble_step ($3671).

0, 3, 6 ... 60: the offset of each of the 21 lines of a sprite shape (3 bytes a line). bubble_scroll reads them as `ldx $3596,y` with Y = $EB-$FF ($050C), to rotate line Y's bytes across the 8 bubble sprites.

Zeroes the sprite text panel's shapes $10-$27 ($4400-$49FF). Called from the title code at $2924 (jump) and $2E5A, and by the menu ($E33C, $E8DE by byte search; $E612, $E6B0, $E70A, $E7B3 in its decoded code).

Starts printing text_ptr's text in the speech bubble: jumps to text_decode, which follows the control bytes up to the first letter and sets up its glyph; the bubble's interrupt routine (bubble_step) then draws it a pixel at a time and reads on. 14 callers in the title code and the menu at $E33F and $E8EC (byte search). The text ends at `$7F`, which sets step_done.

Sets up bubble glyph X: its 21-byte columns from $A82D/$A87B[X], its width in pixels from $A753[X] (11 for the space, X = $DF); clears text_bit_count and loads the glyph's first column into bubble_glyph_column ($1B7B, 21 bytes), or zeroes for a space. Entered from char_to_glyph.
Operand of `lda $FFFF,x` at $36DA: the glyph's current 21-byte column, set from $A82D/$A87B ($36B6/$36BC) and moved 21 bytes per 8 pixels ($3701-$370F).
High byte of the glyph column's address; the code after it copies its 21 bytes, or for a space clears the column buffer.

Counts one pixel of the current glyph: when its width (text_glyph_columns) runs out, reads the next character (text_ptr_next, text_decode); after 8 pixels loads the glyph's next column (text_glyph_row counted, source +21). Called from bubble_step ($3676).
Control byte `$F3 n`: saves the return (text_ptr_save) and continues at string n of the table $B162/$B16B ("one" ... "nine", for the Quickfire question count).
Control byte `$F0 n`: raises event n for the round code (text_event_arg = n, text_event = $FF) and reads on.

Control byte `$F2 n`: saves the return and continues at string n of the table $AB8D/$AB93 (the subjects "Pop", "Rock", "Rock 'n' Roll", "Country & Folk", "Classical", "Mystery"); n at $B325 is set to the question's subject.
Control byte `$FF`, the end of a called string: continues at text_return ($F4/$F5). There is one return address, so a `$7D` call inside a called string cannot return twice.
Control byte `$FE`, the end of a name: continues at name_return ($3402/$3403).

The printer's reader: the byte at text_ptr is a control byte ($F0 event, $F1 name, $F2/$F3 table strings, $FF return, $FE name return, $7E goto, $7D call, $7C wait for fire, $7F end) or a character for char_to_glyph. 10 jumps return here after a control byte.
Control byte `$F1 n`: inserts name n: name_return = the byte after n, text_ptr = the name table's entry n ($AE98/$AEA7, operands $37B5/$37BA).

Operand of `lda $AE98,x` at $37B4: the low bytes of the name table. The menu's code at $CBF8-$CC09 rewrites these four operands to $1D28 and $1D2F, the title's own name table (the picked players' names).
High byte of the name table's low-byte list ($AE in the snapshot, $1D after the menu's $CBFF).
Operand of `lda $AEA7,x` at $37B9: the name table's high bytes, low byte of their address ($2F after the menu's $CC04).
High byte of the address of the name table's high bytes ($AE, then $1D after $CC09).

Control byte `$7C`: waits for fire from either player: reads player one's input (team = 0, read_input) and then player two's (team = 1); on fire (bit 4 clear) reads on; else sets wait_fire_flag and returns, and bubble_step calls here again each pixel. Leaves team at the player who pressed, or 1. Used in the game-over text ($B43B).
Control byte `$7E lo hi`: continues at the address (a goto, no return).
Control byte `$7D lo hi`: saves the return (text_ptr_save, after the operand) and continues at the address; the string's `$FF` comes back.
Control byte `$7F`: sets step_done ($FF) and returns, so the round code waiting on it goes on.

Maps a character to its bubble glyph and calls set_glyph: "=" $4D, "." $3A, "&" $4B, "/" $4C, "-" and ":" $4A, "?" $3B, "," $3C, "(" $3D (an opening quotation mark), ")" $3E (a closing one), "'" $3F, "0"-"9" $40-$49, any other code less $41: "A"-"Z" 0-25, "a"-"z" 32-57, the space $DF (drawn as 11 blank pixels).
Low bytes of the four score-digit sprite shapes $4200, $4240, $4280, $42C0 (shapes 8-11: team 0 tens and units, team 1 tens and units); read by score_digits_frame at $1EE0.
High bytes of the four score-digit shapes ($42 each); read at $1EE9.
Team 0's score as its digits show it, BCD: 0 from scores_reset ($0EDC); while it differs from score_0 ($1F36) score_digits_frame adds 1 every 16 frames ($1F4A-$1F50) as the digits roll.
Team 1's score as shown, BCD: reset $0EDF, compared $1FC4, counted up $1FD8-$1FDE.

Team 0's score in BCD (two digits): 0 at a new game ($0ED6), points added by award_points ($30EF-$30F5); read by the computer's answer choice ($093C, $0966: is it behind?), the score roll ($1F33) and game_over ($27EB).
Team 1's score in BCD: reset $0ED9, added at $30FD-$3103, read $093F, $0969, $1FC1, $27EE.
pick_question's group (its A on entry, $2C76), reloaded into X for each redraw ($2C79).

Show step 7, Spot the Star for team 1: the round's screen, text $B1FB ("<team 1's captain>'s team ... who is this famous star ?"), $AF3A = 2 (team 1's captain's picture, drawn by ask_question_body); on the text's event hides the left team (hide_left_team); at its end spot_the_star_pick.

Show step 6, Spot the Star for team 0: the round's screen, text $B203 ("The next round is (Spot the Star). <team 0's captain>'s team who is this famous star ?"), $AF3A = 1; on the event hides the right team (hide_right_team); then spot_the_star_pick.

Round type 2 (Spot the Star), both_teams_answer off; picks one of the section's 8 stars not yet used (a random bit of round_bits against items_used_2 $1DAF, which only block_choice clears: two stars a game, four games a block) into question_number; tries_left 2, 3 points, ask_question. The clues come one by one, a point less each ($2FC6-$2FDD).
Show step 8: text_ptr = $3E03 (the round's announcement, then the turn's text at $B452) and your_scene_question.
Show steps 9-13: text_ptr = $B43F ("Your scene round - <name> will you please ...") and your_scene_question.

One Your Scene turn: clears the colours and 150 bitmap cells from $6428, draws the frame and the teams, prints the text; the turn's player (turn_players) goes into $AF3A and the text's arguments $B453/$B455, and that player's specialist subject (team_subjects $0B0B + player - 1, read as $0B0A,Y) into your_scene_subject; two_choices_flag set. On the text's event lights only that player. Then the choice "Easy" / "or" / "Hard" (print_text 36-38) beside the subject's icon (colour_face_block at column subject_icon_column[team], row 3, highlighted), the computer's moves set, display state 11 until fire, flash_choice. Points = choice + 1; Easy keeps the player's subject, Hard takes a random other one of the six; the subject goes into the text's `$F2` argument ($B325) and pick_question picks the question; your_scene_subject then holds the choice (0 Easy, 1 Hard) for the lead-in at $2E20. Then ask_question.
A random subject 0-5 (redrawn until below 6) into the text's subject argument $B325, then pick_question. Called by quickfire_start ($0DB6) and quickfire_next ($0DE9).

Your Scene: the asked player's specialist subject (0-5, $399A), read by the subject icon ($3A4E), the Easy choice ($3A97) and the Hard choice's "not the same" test ($3AA6); after the choice it holds 0 (Easy) or 1 (Hard) ($3AB6), which ask_again reads ($2E20) to say "An Easy" or "A Hard question on".
Copies the 1 KB at $F800-$FBFF into colour RAM ($D800-$DBFF). Called by the menu at $E342 (byte search); no caller in the title code.

For round types 0 and 3 (from ask_again at $2E3B; other types return at $28BF): shuffles the slots (shuffle_answers), writes the right answer (the string after the question's $FF, from build_question's $343C) into slot $3506, then reads the 4 bytes after the answer's $FF: the flags byte (wrong_answer_flags) and three references, one per wrong answer for slots $3507-$3509. A flag bit set takes the reference as a string number in the spare list (find_spare_answer); clear, as a question number whose answer is borrowed (find_question, then skip_to_ff past that question's text). Then irq_exit_port back to $25, waits until an interrupt has left $01 with I/O ($01 & 7 = 5) and turns the state interrupt back on (second_irq_on).
Moves the pointer at $3C16/$3C17 (its own `lda` operand) forward to the next $FF. 3 callers in build_answers ($3B5F, $3BAB, $3BEA).
Operand of `lda $FFFF` at $3C15: skip_to_ff's pointer, low byte; build_answers sets it to a question's start and reads it back, +1, as that question's answer ($3B4A-$3B66, $3B96-$3BB2, $3BE2-$3BF1).
High byte of skip_to_ff's pointer ($3B4F, $3B9B, $3BE7; carried at $3C25-$3C2A).
Low bytes of the four 23-byte answer buffers $1BBA, $1BD1, $1BE8, $1BFF (answers A-D), by slot; read by write_answer at $3C3A.
High bytes of the four answer buffers ($1B each), read at $3C52.
write_answer's position in the buffer, kept across find_word ($3C82, $3C97, $3C9A).

Writes the answer string at zp_ptr_2A into answer buffer X (slot 0-3, answer_buffer_lo/hi), patching the buffer into seven operands: plain bytes copied; a byte $80 + n becomes word n of the word list (find_word) with a space before it unless one is there and a space after it; the $FF is copied as the end; the first letter made capital. Returns with $3C77/$3C78 on the answer's $FF. No length check: a buffer is 23 bytes. 8 callers: build_clue_question ($27A3-$27D3) and build_answers ($3B0B-$3BFF).
Operand of `lda $FFFF` at $3C76: write_answer's source pointer (from zp_ptr_2A, $3C6C/$3C71), +1 a byte; left on the answer's $FF for build_answers ($3B0E, $3B24).
High byte of write_answer's source pointer (read by build_answers at $3B16, $3B2C).
Operand of `lda $FFFF,x` at $3C8A: the answer buffer, to test the character before a word for a space.
High byte of that buffer address ($3C5E).
Operand of `sta $FFFF,x` at $3C94: the answer buffer, to put a space before a word.
High byte of that buffer address; the code after it finds the word (find_word) and points the copy at it.
Operand of `lda $FFFF,y` at $3CAC: the word being copied into the answer (from find_word, $3CA2/$3CA7).
High byte of the word's address.
Operand of `sta $FFFF,x` at $3CB8: the answer buffer, for a word's letters.
High byte of that buffer address ($3C55).
Operand of `sta $FFFF,x` at $3CC0: the answer buffer, for plain bytes and the space after a word.
High byte of that buffer address; the code after it steps the source and loops.
Operand of `sta $FFFF,x` at $3CD8: the answer buffer, for the end byte $FF.
High byte of that buffer address.
Operand of `lda $FFFF` at $3CDB: the buffer's first character, made a capital if it is a small letter.
High byte of the first character's address.
Operand of `sta $FFFF` at $3CE5: where the capital letter is written back (the buffer's start).
High byte of that address.
answer_flash_frame's frame counter, 0-2: every third frame the colour moves on ($3D1C-$3D2B). The menu's copy of the routine uses it too ($E55D-$E569, decoded by agent 1's xrefs).
The position in the team's colour list ($3D2B-$3D3A); also used by the menu ($E56C-$E57B).
flash_choice's count of busy-loop delays, 2 ($31C0, $31CD); also the menu ($E57E, $EA40).
Where each team's colours start in team_flash_colours: 0 for team 0, 7 for team 1. Read by answer_flash_frame ($3CFE) and the grid cursor's colour cycle ($180D).

Two colour lists ending $FF: team 0 2, 10, 7, 1, 7, 10 (red, light red, yellow, white); team 1 6, 14, 3, 1, 3, 14 (blue, light blue, cyan, white). Read at $3D31 and by the grid cursor's cycle ($182E, $1835).

Display state 10, once a frame (from the state table at $06CB/$06DA): flashes the team's chosen answer through its colour list (a step every third frame), the other answers' bars black: four answer bars (fill_colour_block), or the two of Easy or Hard (two_choice_highlight, when two_choices_flag is set); then the sprite text panel (sprites_row0).
Operand of `lda $3CEE,y` at $3D31: the team's colour list (flash_colours + team_flash_start, $3D04/$3D0B).
